cases.question: For each customer who bought a home product in a completed order, count distinct completed orders containing a home product.
cases.generated_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS completed_orders_with_home_product
FROM customers AS c
JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products AS p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.status = 'completed'
  AND p.category = 'home'
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name

reconstructed_visible_intent.population: matching-only customers with completed orders containing a home product

reference_sql.a: SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS home_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.category = 'home' GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY c.customer_id
reference_sql.b: WITH home_orders AS (SELECT DISTINCT o.customer_id, o.order_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.category = 'home') SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS home_orders FROM home_orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY customer_id

fixtures.purpose: Adds two home lines to one order, distinguishing distinct orders from line count.
Adds a pending home order that must not enter the population.

cases.first_divergence: The model adds c.customer_name to SELECT and GROUP BY although the requested result is the customer identifier plus the count. The path, filters, distinct count, and grouping key are otherwise correct.
cases.evidence_used_incorrectly: The visible stable customer identifier was used, but the model also projected the visible display name that the question did not request.
cases.benchmark_review_reason: The question does not explicitly enumerate or prohibit display columns; the minimal identifier-plus-measure projection is an implicit benchmark convention.

cases.question: For each route, calculate rounded average kilometres per litre across its trips, excluding zero-fuel ratios.
cases.generated_sql: SELECT r.route_id, r.route_code, r.route_name, ROUND(AVG(t.distance_km / NULLIF(t.fuel_liters, 0)), 2) AS average_kilometres_per_litre FROM routes AS r JOIN trips AS t ON t.route_id = r.route_id GROUP BY r.route_id, r.route_code, r.route_name

reconstructed_visible_intent.filter_scope: zero fuel excluded inside the row ratio via NULLIF
reconstructed_visible_intent.aggregate: average of trip-level distance/fuel ratios, rounded for display

reference_sql.a: SELECT r.route_id, ROUND(AVG(t.distance_km / NULLIF(t.fuel_liters, 0))::numeric, 2) AS km_per_liter FROM routes r JOIN trips t ON t.route_id = r.route_id GROUP BY r.route_id ORDER BY r.route_id
reference_sql.b: WITH ratios AS (SELECT route_id, distance_km / NULLIF(fuel_liters, 0) AS ratio FROM trips) SELECT r.route_id, ROUND(AVG(ratios.ratio)::numeric, 2) AS km_per_liter FROM routes r JOIN ratios ON ratios.route_id = r.route_id GROUP BY r.route_id ORDER BY r.route_id

fixtures.purpose: Adds zero fuel, proving the NULLIF exclusion rule.
Adds differing ratios to distinguish average ratio from ratio of averages.

cases.first_divergence: The metric expression is correct, but the model returns route_code and route_name in addition to route_id and the requested metric.
cases.evidence_used_incorrectly: The route identifier was supplemented with display attributes not requested by the question.
cases.aggregation_forensics: CORRECT row-ratio then average; NULLIF excludes zero fuel
cases.benchmark_review_reason: The natural-language phrase 'for each route' does not explicitly say route_id only, while route_code and route_name are visible attributes.

cases.question: For each driver, count trips made in cargo vehicles, returning only drivers with at least one such trip.
cases.generated_sql:
SELECT d.driver_id, d.driver_name, COUNT(t.trip_id) AS cargo_trip_count
FROM drivers AS d
JOIN trips AS t ON t.driver_id = d.driver_id
JOIN vehicles AS v ON v.vehicle_id = t.vehicle_id
WHERE v.vehicle_class = 'cargo'
GROUP BY d.driver_id, d.driver_name
HAVING COUNT(t.trip_id) >= 1

reconstructed_visible_intent.population: drivers with at least one cargo-vehicle trip

reference_sql.a: SELECT d.driver_id, COUNT(t.trip_id) AS cargo_trips FROM drivers d JOIN trips t ON t.driver_id = d.driver_id JOIN vehicles v ON v.vehicle_id = t.vehicle_id WHERE v.vehicle_class = 'cargo' GROUP BY d.driver_id ORDER BY d.driver_id
reference_sql.b: WITH cargo AS (SELECT t.driver_id FROM trips t JOIN vehicles v ON v.vehicle_id = t.vehicle_id WHERE v.vehicle_class = 'cargo') SELECT d.driver_id, COUNT(*) AS cargo_trips FROM drivers d JOIN cargo ON cargo.driver_id = d.driver_id GROUP BY d.driver_id ORDER BY d.driver_id

fixtures.purpose: Adds a cargo trip for a driver who otherwise has only non-cargo trips.
Adds a van trip that must not enter cargo counts.

cases.first_divergence: The model adds driver_name to the requested driver_id and cargo-trip count; the joins, cargo predicate, count, and matching-only population are correct.
cases.evidence_used_incorrectly: The stable driver identifier was supplemented with the visible display name.
cases.aggregation_forensics: CORRECT count; HAVING is redundant but equivalent after the cargo WHERE
cases.benchmark_review_reason: The question identifies the entity as a driver but does not explicitly enumerate the projection columns.

cases.question: For every vehicle with telemetry, return its latest telemetry timestamp and documented engine temperature; if timestamps tie, use the highest event ID, and list vehicles by vehicle ID.
cases.generated_sql:
SELECT v.vehicle_id, t.event_at AS latest_telemetry_timestamp, t.payload #>> '{engine,temperature_c}' AS engine_temperature_c
FROM vehicles AS v
JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (vehicle_id)
           vehicle_id,
           event_at,
           payload
    FROM telemetry_events
    ORDER BY vehicle_id, event_at DESC, event_id DESC
) AS t ON t.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
ORDER BY v.vehicle_id;

sql_decomposition.subquery: DISTINCT ON (vehicle_id) ordered by event_at DESC, event_id DESC

reconstructed_visible_intent.filter_scope: latest row per vehicle, no extra row filter
reconstructed_visible_intent.temporal: event_at DESC with event_id DESC tie-break

reference_sql.a: SELECT vehicle_id, event_at, temperature_c FROM (SELECT vehicle_id, event_at, (payload #>> '{engine,temperature_c}')::numeric AS temperature_c, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY vehicle_id ORDER BY event_at DESC, event_id DESC) AS rn FROM telemetry_events) AS latest WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY vehicle_id
reference_sql.b: SELECT t.vehicle_id, t.event_at, (t.payload #>> '{engine,temperature_c}')::numeric AS temperature_c FROM telemetry_events t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM telemetry_events newer WHERE newer.vehicle_id = t.vehicle_id AND (newer.event_at, newer.event_id) > (t.event_at, t.event_id)) ORDER BY t.vehicle_id

fixtures.purpose: Adds a later reading for vehicle 1 and an older reading for vehicle 2.
Adds equal-timestamp events, proving the event ID tie-break is part of the result.

cases.first_divergence: The documented JSON path and latest-row ordering are correct, but #>> returns text and the model omits the required ::numeric coercion for the NUMERIC attribute. The first base mismatch is therefore typed output, not latest-row selection.
cases.evidence_used_incorrectly: The physical JSON path was used, but the visible NUMERIC data type was not carried into the projection.
cases.temporal_forensics: CORRECT event_at DESC and event_id DESC tie-break

cases.question: For every account, count urgent support tickets, including accounts with zero urgent tickets.
cases.generated_sql:
SELECT a.account_id, a.account_name, COUNT(st.ticket_id) FILTER (WHERE st.priority = 'urgent') AS urgent_ticket_count
FROM accounts AS a
LEFT JOIN support_tickets AS st ON st.account_id = a.account_id
GROUP BY a.account_id, a.account_name
ORDER BY a.account_id

reconstructed_visible_intent.population: all accounts, preserving accounts with zero urgent tickets
reconstructed_visible_intent.filter_scope: conditional aggregate filter, not query WHERE

reference_sql.a: SELECT a.account_id, COUNT(t.ticket_id) FILTER (WHERE t.priority = 'urgent') AS urgent_tickets FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN support_tickets t ON t.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.account_id ORDER BY a.account_id
reference_sql.b: WITH urgent AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS urgent_tickets FROM support_tickets WHERE priority = 'urgent' GROUP BY account_id) SELECT a.account_id, COALESCE(urgent.urgent_tickets, 0)::BIGINT FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN urgent ON urgent.account_id = a.account_id ORDER BY a.account_id

fixtures.purpose: Adds an account with no tickets and one normal ticket.
Adds an urgent and normal ticket for one account, distinguishing FILTER from WHERE.

cases.first_divergence: The model correctly preserves all accounts and scopes urgent to FILTER, but adds account_name to the two-column requested result.
cases.evidence_used_incorrectly: The account display name was added even though the question asks for the count per account and the canonical output is account_id plus count.
cases.aggregation_forensics: CORRECT FILTER scope and COUNT(ticket_id) NULL behavior
cases.benchmark_review_reason: The question does not explicitly enumerate account_id as the only account identifier or prohibit account_name.

cases.question: List tickets whose first agent response exceeded the first-response SLA of the account's most recently started subscription.
cases.generated_sql: SELECT t.ticket_id, t.account_id, t.opened_at, r.first_response_at, sp.first_response_sla_hours, r.first_response_at - t.opened_at AS first_response_time FROM support_tickets AS t JOIN accounts AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.account_id) s.account_id, s.plan_id FROM subscriptions AS s ORDER BY s.account_id, s.starts_on DESC, s.subscription_id DESC) AS latest_sub ON latest_sub.account_id = a.account_id JOIN service_plans AS sp ON sp.plan_id = latest_sub.plan_id JOIN (SELECT t2.ticket_id, MIN(e.event_at) AS first_response_at FROM support_tickets AS t2 JOIN ticket_events AS e ON e.ticket_id = t2.ticket_id WHERE e.event_type = 'agent_response' AND e.event_at > t2.opened_at GROUP BY t2.ticket_id) AS r ON r.ticket_id = t.ticket_id WHERE r.first_response_at > t.opened_at + sp.first_response_sla_hours * INTERVAL '1 hour'

reconstructed_visible_intent.population: tickets with a first agent response strictly after the applicable SLA
reconstructed_visible_intent.relationship_path: tickets -> accounts <- subscriptions -> service_plans; ticket_events -> tickets
reconstructed_visible_intent.filter_scope: MIN agent_response after opened_at, then strict SLA comparison
reconstructed_visible_intent.temporal: most recently started subscription; first response; lower boundary exclusive

reference_sql.a: SELECT t.ticket_id FROM support_tickets t JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT ON (account_id) account_id, plan_id FROM subscriptions ORDER BY account_id, starts_on DESC, subscription_id DESC) s ON s.account_id = t.account_id JOIN service_plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id JOIN (SELECT ticket_id, MIN(event_at) AS first_response_at FROM ticket_events WHERE event_type = 'agent_response' GROUP BY ticket_id) e ON e.ticket_id = t.ticket_id WHERE e.first_response_at > t.opened_at + p.first_response_sla_hours * INTERVAL '1 hour' ORDER BY t.ticket_id
reference_sql.b: SELECT t.ticket_id FROM support_tickets t WHERE (SELECT MIN(e.event_at) FROM ticket_events e WHERE e.ticket_id = t.ticket_id AND e.event_type = 'agent_response') > t.opened_at + (SELECT p.first_response_sla_hours * INTERVAL '1 hour' FROM subscriptions s JOIN service_plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id WHERE s.account_id = t.account_id ORDER BY s.starts_on DESC LIMIT 1) ORDER BY t.ticket_id

fixtures.purpose: Adds a ticket at and just after the SLA boundary.
Adds an unanswered ticket; NULL first response must not be a breach.
Adds a later subscription with a stricter SLA.

cases.first_divergence: The observable SLA query logic matches the references, but the model returns five diagnostic columns in addition to the requested ticket_id.
semantic_diff: + SELECT t.ticket_id, t.account_id, t.opened_at, r.first_response_at, sp.first_response_sla_hours, ...
cases.evidence_used_incorrectly: No required SLA evidence was misapplied; the model exposed intermediate values that were not requested.

relationship_forensics.unnecessary_relationship: JOIN accounts is not needed once ticket.account_id is available, but it is authorized and not semantically wrong.

cases.temporal_forensics: CORRECT latest subscription, first response, strict boundary
cases.benchmark_review_reason: The question explicitly names tickets but does not explicitly say that only ticket_id may be returned.

cases.question: For each account with tickets, report the urgent-ticket share rounded to four decimals.
cases.generated_sql: SELECT a.account_id, a.account_name, ROUND(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.priority = 'urgent')::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 4) AS urgent_ticket_share FROM accounts AS a JOIN support_tickets AS t ON t.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.account_id, a.account_name

reconstructed_visible_intent.population: accounts with at least one ticket
reconstructed_visible_intent.filter_scope: urgent predicate only in numerator FILTER
reconstructed_visible_intent.aggregate: urgent ticket count divided by all ticket count, rounded to four decimals

reference_sql.a: SELECT account_id, ROUND((COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE priority = 'urgent'))::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 4) AS urgent_share FROM support_tickets GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY account_id
reference_sql.b: WITH counts AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE priority = 'urgent') AS urgent FROM support_tickets GROUP BY account_id) SELECT account_id, ROUND((urgent::numeric / NULLIF(total, 0)), 4) AS urgent_share FROM counts ORDER BY account_id

fixtures.purpose: Adds three tickets with one urgent to distinguish row-level ratio from aggregate ratio mistakes.
Adds a normal-only account to test population and NULL behavior.

cases.first_divergence: The ratio formula, denominator, inner population, and rounding are correct; the model adds account_name to the requested account_id and share.
cases.evidence_used_incorrectly: The account display name was projected even though only the account-level share was requested.
cases.aggregation_forensics: CORRECT post-count ratio and display-only rounding
cases.benchmark_review_reason: The question says for each account but does not explicitly enumerate the identifier column or exclude account_name.

cases.question: Find accounts with at least one ticket whose ticket count is above the average count among accounts with at least one ticket.
cases.generated_sql:
SELECT a.account_id, a.account_name, tc.ticket_count
FROM accounts AS a
JOIN (
    SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
    FROM support_tickets
    GROUP BY account_id
) AS tc ON tc.account_id = a.account_id
WHERE tc.ticket_count > (
    SELECT AVG(ticket_count)
    FROM (
        SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
        FROM support_tickets
        GROUP BY account_id
    ) AS counts
)
ORDER BY a.account_id

reconstructed_visible_intent.population: accounts with at least one ticket; zero-ticket accounts excluded from the baseline average
reconstructed_visible_intent.relationship_path: none required; account_id is the grouping key
reconstructed_visible_intent.filter_scope: compare each per-account count to the average of those counts
reconstructed_visible_intent.aggregate: COUNT per account then AVG of per-account counts

reference_sql.a: WITH counts AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS ticket_count FROM support_tickets GROUP BY account_id), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(ticket_count) AS average_count FROM counts) SELECT account_id, ticket_count FROM counts, baseline WHERE ticket_count > baseline.average_count ORDER BY account_id
reference_sql.b: SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS ticket_count FROM support_tickets GROUP BY account_id HAVING COUNT(*) > (SELECT AVG(ticket_count) FROM (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS ticket_count FROM support_tickets GROUP BY account_id) AS per_account) ORDER BY account_id

fixtures.purpose: Adds a burst of tickets to one account, making above-average membership observable.
Adds a no-ticket cohort; those accounts must not be part of the per-account average.

cases.first_divergence: The nested population and above-average comparison are correct, but the model adds account_name to the requested account_id and ticket_count.
cases.evidence_used_incorrectly: The model added a display attribute despite correctly using only ticket-bearing accounts for the baseline.
cases.population_forensics: CORRECT matching-only and filtered denominator population
cases.benchmark_review_reason: The question does not explicitly enumerate the account projection columns; account_name is visible and plausibly useful but not part of the canonical target.
